title: Private Network Policy Terraform Module (SG + NACL + Private DNS + Egress Controls)
creator: Priya Singh
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that codifies Redwood's recommended network security posture for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will manage security groups, network ACLs, private Route 53 hosted zones and records, and opinionated egress controls (deny-by-default with explicit allow lists and optional NAT/egress VPC endpoints). It must be parameterizable for customer VPCs (CIDR, public/private subnets, NAT vs egress-via-endpoints), support both IPv4 and IPv6 patterns, and include automated health checks and observability hooks (VPC Flow Logs, Route 53 health checks).
background: We currently have ad-hoc terraform snippets across several private deployment repos. Customers and platform teams need a single well-documented module that enforces least-privilege egress and consistent private DNS patterns for internal services. This reduces misconfigurations during onboarding and enables safer automated upgrades of private deployments.
scope: Implement terraform module and tests. Provide examples for three common topologies: 1) fully private (no internet egress except via managed NAT), 2) private with limited egress via VPC endpoints, 3) mixed environment with controlled public proxies. Add CI checks and a canary upgrade path. Include docs and migration steps for older stacks.
out_of_scope: Billing or quota management, application-level firewall rules (WAF), or implementing customer-specific proxy appliances. Integration with third-party DNS providers is out of scope for initial release.
deliverables: automated terratest suite and CI pipeline (PR checks)
Confluence design and runbook for troubleshooting
upgrade/migration guide for existing private deployments
acceptance_criteria: Module is published in our private terraform registry with semver and README
Module creates Security Groups and NACLs that implement deny-by-default egress and explicit allow rules when configured
Private Route 53 hosted zone and required records can be optionally created and attached to the VPC
Module supports toggles for NAT vs VPC endpoints and documents cost/latency tradeoffs
End-to-end terratest runs pass in CI against a sandbox AWS account
Module includes automated health check resources (Route 53 health checks or CloudWatch synthetic checks) with remediation playbook
Observability hooks: VPC Flow Logs to S3/CloudWatch and CloudTrail guidance included
implementation_notes: Use explicit inputs: allowed_egress_cidrs, allowed_egress_ports, endpoints_map (service -> interface/gateway), enable_ipv6
Security Groups: prefer minimal role-based SGs for control plane and data plane with tags for automated lifecycle management
NACLs: stateless layer to limit blast radius for cross-AZ traffic; default to open for intra-subnet traffic only when explicitly allowed
Private DNS: create Route 53 private hosted zone when create_private_dns=true; emit example records for service discovery (registrar pattern)
Egress policy: default deny egress; provide allow-lists and optional use of a central egress proxy via pivot security group
Upgrades: follow semver; include migration helpers that add new rules via additional resources to avoid drift during in-place upgrades
Testing: terratest + terraform plan diff assertions; nightly drift detection via a scheduled job
testing_and_health_checks: Route 53 health checks for internal critical endpoints (api-ingress, metadata-proxy)
Synthetic connectivity checks from a sandbox instance to allowed egress targets
CI: terraform validate, fmt, tflint, and terratest integration in pipeline
Monitor VPC Flow Logs for blocked egress attempts and surface actionable alerts to Console
Create a small lambda-based canary that verifies DNS resolution of private hosted zone after changes
rollout_plan: 1. Merge module into registry with v0.1.0 and examples in examples/v0.1
2. Run terratest in sandbox account and validate logs for 72h
3. Pilot with 2 internal private deployments (staging + infra-team) for a week
4. Create migration PR templates for customer repos and schedule staggered upgrades
5. After pilot success, promote to v1.0.0 and add to onboarding templates
rollback_plan: If upgrade causes blocked egress or DNS failures, revert to prior registry version and apply immediately
Keep a documented emergency ruleset (temp-allow-egress) that operators can apply via the Console or terraform to restore connectivity
Use automated runbook: capture terraform plan output, escalate to SRE on-call, run remediation script to patch security group rules
